Present: Mr. Vipin Mahajan, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. Mohit Chaudhary, Aag, Punjab.
Mr. Nitish Bhatia, Advocate for the complainant.
Sandeep Moudgil, J (Qral)

The instant
petition under Section 438 Cr.P.C., has been filed for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner in
Fir No.145, dated 10.12.2015, under Sections 420 & 120-B of the Ipc, 1860, registered at Police
Station City Fazilka, District Fazilka, Punjab.

This Court vide order dated 09.02.2023, granted interim protection to the petitioner and the parties
are directed to appear before the Mediation & Conciliation Centre of this Court after having consent
of both the parties.
Finally, the mediation has succeeded and the settlement agreement dated 16.03.2023 has been entered between the parties.
According to which, a demand draft of Rs.55,000/- to be paid as full and final payment to resolve the dispute for forever.

A perusal of the terms of agreement crystallized as under:

sentences.text: 2. Pursuant to this FIR the parties met in the good office of SP(D) District, Fazilka, where a compromise was arrived at and sum of Rs.1,15,000/- (One Lakh fifteen thousand only) was paid to the second party.
Subsequently, the second party raised demand of Rs.85,000/- (Eighty Five Thousand) for which the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre vide order dated 09.02.2023 passed by this Hon'ble Court.

3. Detailed discussions were held with the parties and now, the parties have, with the intervention of learned advocates of both the parties voluntarily arrived at an amicable solution resolving their disputes and differences.

In addition to the already paid amount of Rs.1,15,000/- (One Lakh Fifteen Thousand) the first party undertakes to make another amount of Rs.55,000/-(Fifty Five Thousand)
as full and final payment so as to resolve the pending dispute.

This amount of Rs.55,000/- (Fifty Five Thousand) shallbe paid by way of demand draft in the name of second party or in cash before this Hon'ble Court on 22.03.2023 when the present petition is fixed for hearing.
A quashing petition pertaining to this FIR is also pending before the Hon'ble Court for 22.03.2023.

On receiving the balance amount of Rs.55,000/- (fifty Five thousand) second party to undertakes to MEENU 2023.03.23 09:36 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document MEENU 2023.03.23 09:36 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document make a statement to this effect and give no objection in case of quashing of the FIR by this Hon'ble Court as his entire amount stands paid.

4. The parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free will arrived at this Settlement/Agreement in the presence of the Mediator. . That this is the full and final settlement between the parties regarding their financial dispute.

None of the parties will claim over and above the present settled amount. . That the parties shall not breach the terms of settlement and if any party goes out of the terms of settlement then the other party shall have a right to take course of law.
7.

By signing this Agreement the parties hereto state that they have no further claims or demands against each other and all the disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the parties hereto through the process of Conciliation/Mediation and the parties shall not institute any other case against each other will respect to the present claim.
Both the parties also undertakes not to initiate any further litigation on the same subject matter in future.
. That the parties undertake before this Hon'ble Court to abide by the terms and conditions set out in the agreement and not to dispute the same hereinafter in future.

. That the parties to this agreement hereby state that they have read the agreement, that they have understood the contents thereof and their execution of agreement is voluntarily.
10.By execution of this agreement, each _ signatory acknowledges receipt of fully executed duplicate/original of this agreement.

sentences.text: That it has been further agreed between the parties that in case of necessity, both the parties shall be free to present the copy of the above compromise before any authority or Court if the same is required to witness the execution of the compromise or to settle any pending controversy between the parties.

In compliance to the above, it is clearly evident that both the parties have agreed that out of the dispute, an amount of Rs.1,15,000/- was paid earlier to the second party and another demand of Rs.85,000/- was made, which has now been settled with the support of the Mediator Dr. Amarpreet Kaur Sandhu in Rs.55,000/- as full and final settlement.

In view of the same, a demand draft of Rs.55,000/- bearing No.001124 dated 21.03.2023 drawn at Bandhan Bank in favour of the complainant has been produced in the Court, which has been handed over to learned counsel appearing on behalf of the complainant.
It has been further stated by the learned State counsel that the petitioner has joined the investigation on 27.02.2023 and not required for further custodial interrogation.

Be that as it may, in view of the settlement arrived between the parties before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court dated 16.03.2023, no purpose would be served by keeping the petition pending.
Hence, the order dated 09.02.2023 is made absolute.
Accordingly, the present petition stands disposed of.
(SANDEEP MOUDGIL)
